scope_note: Intel’s Xeon E5-2600 v4 family (Broadwell-EP) is the document’s covered server product family; dated Intel investor-relations release identifies the 2016 announcement.
source_quote: Intel® Xeon® processor E5-2600 v4 product family delivers the foundation for modern, software-defined clouds.
date_basis: Dated Intel release associates E5-2600 v4 with the March 31, 2016 product announcement; this plot uses the introduction year.

scope_note: The specification update covers the first Xeon Scalable family, codenamed Skylake-SP; Intel’s developer overview identifies the new generation as formerly Skylake-SP and states the Xeon Scalable platform launched that year.
source_quote: This year, Intel launched the highly anticipated Intel® Xeon® platform.
date_basis: Year-only evidence in this source; Intel source title/specification-update mapping identifies the Scalable family, and the technical overview identifies Skylake-SP as its codename.

scope_note: 2nd Gen Xeon Scalable processors are Cascade Lake; this official Intel release says they were released and generally available on April 2, 2019.
source_quote: Available today, Intel released 2nd-Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors.
date_basis: Intel’s release records general availability April 2, 2019; this is the clearest commercial availability date for the named family.

scope_note: The input document covers 3rd Gen Xeon Scalable (server Ice Lake), not the client Ice Lake family.
source_quote: Intel today launched its most advanced, highest performance data center platform.
date_basis: The same release identifies 3rd Gen Xeon Scalable as Ice Lake and dates launch April 6, 2021.

scope_note: 4th Gen Xeon Scalable is codenamed Sapphire Rapids; the source release is the January 2023 launch notice.
source_quote: Intel today marked one of the most important product launches in company history with the unveiling of 4th Gen Intel® Xeon® Scalable processors.
date_basis: Intel’s release dates the launch announcement Jan. 10, 2023; no separate availability date is used in the supplied exact date.

scope_note: 5th Gen Intel Xeon / Xeon Scalable is codenamed Emerald Rapids; this is the server product family in the input source.
source_quote: Intel launched its 5th Gen Intel® Xeon® processors (code-named Emerald Rapids).
date_basis: Official news release dates launch to Dec. 14, 2023.

scope_note: The update covers 8th- and 9th-generation Core desktop families. The earliest covered Coffee Lake desktop commercial availability is 8th Gen in 2017; the 9th Gen extension followed in 2018.
source_quote: Announced on Sept. 24, 8th Gen Intel® Core™ desktop processors are available to purchase starting today.
date_basis: Commercial availability date for the initial covered 8th Gen desktop products, not the later 9th Gen products in the same specification update.

scope_note: 10th Gen U/Y mobile specification update maps to Ice Lake client, separate from the server Ice Lake-SP family.
source_quote: Today, Intel officially launched 11 new, highly integrated 10th Gen Intel® Core™ processors.
date_basis: Intel dated the release Aug. 1, 2019; first 10th Gen mobile Ice Lake products were launched in this announcement.

scope_note: The specification covers 11th Gen UP3/UP4/H35/H45 mobile Tiger Lake variants; Intel first introduced the mobile family in 2020.
source_quote: Intel launches nine new 11th Gen Intel Core processors with Intel Iris Xe graphics (code-named “Tiger Lake”) on Sept. 2, 2020.
date_basis: The announcement introduces the initial Tiger Lake mobile processors; later H-series products arrived in 2021 but are not earlier.

scope_note: 11th Gen S-series desktop processors are Rocket Lake-S, separate from 11th Gen Tiger Lake mobile.
source_quote: The 11th Gen Intel® Core™ S-series desktop processors (code-named “Rocket Lake-S”) launched worldwide today.
date_basis: Intel dates worldwide launch to March 16, 2021.

scope_note: 12th Gen Intel Core is Alder Lake; the first unlocked desktop processors launched with the family introduction at Intel Innovation.
source_quote: Intel introduced the 12th Gen Intel Core processor family during Intel Innovation on Oct. 27, 2021.
date_basis: Launch/introduction date for the family. Retail availability for initial unlocked desktop SKUs followed in November 2021.

scope_note: The specification update spans 13th and 14th Gen Core. The earliest covered family launch is 13th Gen Raptor Lake in 2022; 14th Gen desktop products followed in 2023.
source_quote: At Intel Innovation on Sept. 27, 2022, Intel revealed its new 13th Gen Intel Core processor family.
date_basis: Date locates the first covered Raptor Lake family launch. The combined specification scope later extends to 14th Gen/Raptor Lake Refresh.

scope_note: Intel Core Ultra mobile processors are the Meteor Lake client family in this specification update.
source_quote: Today at Intel’s “AI Everywhere” event, the company launched its Intel® Core™ Ultra mobile processors.
date_basis: Official Intel release dates launch and global retail availability to Dec. 14, 2023.

scope_note: The input document covers Core Ultra 200V Series, codenamed Lunar Lake.
source_quote: Intel today launched its most efficient family of x86 processors ever, the Intel® Core™ Ultra 200V series processors.
date_basis: Intel introduced/launched the family Sept. 3, 2024; the release says preorders started that day and retail systems were scheduled for Sept. 24.

scope_note: Intel Core Ultra Series 2 specification update maps the initial 200S desktop product family to Arrow Lake-S.
source_quote: On Oct. 10, 2024, Intel launched its Intel® Core™ Ultra 200S desktop processors (codenamed Arrow Lake-S).
date_basis: Family announcement/launch date Oct. 10; Intel press kit says partner systems were to start Oct. 24.

date_basis: Official AMD launch release dates the EPYC 7001/Naples server launch June 20, 2017; scope note preserves that the AMD architecture guide can include non-server products.
